questions.scenario: Your school fest has a local celebrity guest coming over, but it's pure chaos. What are you doing?

options.text: Running around with a walkie-talkie, clearing the crowd, making sure the mic works, and getting the photographers in position.
Monitoring the crowd's mood and keeping a close eye on the back gate just in case the celebrity gets mobbed and needs a quick exit.
Making sure the welcome banner looks absolutely stunning and getting ready to shoot a cinematic slow-mo video of their grand entry for Instagram.
Staying right by the celebrity's side, keeping the annoying teachers away, and making sure the star is happy and comfortable.

questions.scenario: A massive, totally fake rumor spreads about your best friend in school. How do you help them survive this?

options.text: You march down the corridor, confront the kids spreading it, and loudly announce the real truth in front of everyone.
You play detective, secretly trace the rumor back to the exact person who started it, and gather WhatsApp screenshots as solid proof.
You help your friend post a super cool, unbothered, aesthetic story on Instagram to show the haters they don't care at all.
You coach your friend on exactly what to say to the coordinator so their reputation stays spotless and they look like the mature victim.

questions.scenario: Your entire class bunked the PT period to play cricket, and now the Principal is furious. What is your strategy?

options.text: You actively gather everyone in a line outside the office, keeping them quiet and organized before facing the music.
You try to figure out what kind of mood the Principal was in today and quickly prepare a logical excuse to minimize the punishment.
You draft a highly emotional, perfectly worded apology letter on behalf of the class using your best handwriting.
You act as the class representative, step into the office alone, and negotiate with the Principal to give you guys extra homework instead of calling parents.

questions.scenario: Your society is hosting a huge Ganesh Chaturthi or Durga Puja event. What is your unofficial job?

options.text: Managing the chaotic Prasad distribution line, telling people where to stand, and coordinating with the dhol-walas.
Keeping an eye on the noise levels and neighbors' complaints to ensure the police don't show up and stop the music.
Clicking gorgeous, perfectly lit photos of the pandal and writing a beautiful, welcoming caption for the society WhatsApp group.
Schmoozing with the chief guest (like the local MLA) and making sure the society gets maximum VIP funding for next year's event.

questions.scenario: Your friend is starting a new YouTube channel or Instagram page. How do you support them?

options.text: You physically go to all your classmates and tuition friends, grab their phones, and hit 'subscribe' yourself.
You constantly check their analytics, figure out which time of day gets the most views, and analyze why a certain reel flopped.
You design a sleek profile picture, choose the perfect color palette, and make sure their feed's 'vibe' is flawless.
You tell them to collaborate with another popular kid in school to double their followers, planning their long-term growth.

questions.scenario: A rival school starts making fun of your school on a local meme page. What's the battle plan?

options.text: You organize a massive cheering squad at the next inter-school sports match to physically show them who is the boss.
You analyze their memes, find their weak points, and carefully plan a counter-attack that won't get you suspended.
You create a highly savage, beautifully edited comeback video that makes your school look premium and superior.
You decide that ignoring them is the ultimate 'high-status' move and convince your friends to act completely unbothered.

questions.scenario: Your younger sibling throws a massive, embarrassing tantrum in front of visiting relatives. How do you handle it?

options.text: You quickly scoop them up, take them to another room, and immediately distract the relatives by serving snacks.
You mentally scan for the root cause—are they sleepy? hungry?—and silently solve the problem without making a scene.
You make a really funny joke out of it to lighten the tension and completely change the topic of the conversation.
You smoothly promise the sibling a chocolate later if they behave now, perfectly protecting the 'ideal family' image in front of the guests.

questions.scenario: You are on the core committee for the 10th standard farewell party. What is your main focus?

options.text: Being on the ground, running from the stage to the caterer, making sure the DJ starts on time and everyone is dancing.
Anticipating disasters like the AC failing or the food running out, and having a solid backup plan ready just in case.
Designing gorgeous e-invites and making sure the balloon decor and photo-booth look absolutely Pinterest-perfect.
Handling the collected funds, negotiating with the banquet hall manager, and making sure the VIP teachers are treated like royalty.

questions.scenario: You see a massive Twitter/X fight breaking out between two huge Bollywood fan clubs. What is your thought process?

options.text: You wonder how crazy it would be to organize a massive, physical fan meetup outside the actor's house instead of fighting online.
You read through the timeline, trying to trace back exactly which tweet started the fire and who is actually in the wrong.
You judge the poor quality of the memes they are using and think about how you could make a much better hype edit.
You realize that all this online drama is secretly free publicity that will actually increase the actor's next box office collection.

questions.scenario: The local street food vendor (chaat/momo bhaiya) you love is losing customers because of a fake food-poisoning WhatsApp forward. How do you save his business?

options.text: You physically stand at his stall, eat the food loudly, and tell passing aunties that the food is completely safe.
You track down the local society WhatsApp group where the fake forward started and aggressively debunk it with logical proof.
You make a mouth-watering, aesthetic vlog about his food and post it on your city's food review page to rebuild his hype.
You advise him to rebrand, wear a clean chef's hat, put up a '100% Hygienic' board, and slightly increase prices to look premium.

Media_Coordinator.title: The Ground Hustler (Media / Event Coordinator)
Media_Coordinator.primary_match_text: You are a pure action-taker! You thrive in chaotic environments, love dealing with people face-to-face, and have the energy to run the show from the frontlines. You don't just plan events; you make them happen.
Media_Coordinator.day_in_the_life: Running loud press conferences, ensuring journalists get the right soundbites, managing live events, and making sure the spotlight is exactly where it needs to be.
Media_Coordinator.alternative_match_text: Your high energy and people skills would also make you a fantastic Event Manager, Journalist, or TV Producer.
Media_Coordinator.roadmap: 11th/12th: Arts or Commerce. Degree: Bachelor of Mass Media (BMM) or B.A. in Journalism & Mass Communication. Next Steps: Intern heavily with Event Management or PR agencies.

Crisis_Analyst.title: The Damage Controller (Crisis Management Analyst)
Crisis_Analyst.primary_match_text: You are the cool head in a burning room. You are deeply analytical, observant, and naturally good at finding the root cause of a problem. When a reputation is crashing, you are the genius who stops the bleeding.
Crisis_Analyst.day_in_the_life: Tracking social media sentiment, finding out who started a negative rumor about a brand, writing emergency response plans, and saving companies from cancellation.
Crisis_Analyst.alternative_match_text: Your analytical and logical brain makes you a perfect fit for Corporate Law, Data Analytics, or Investigative Journalism.
Crisis_Analyst.roadmap: 11th/12th: Commerce or Arts. Degree: BBA or B.A. in Public Relations / Corporate Communication. Next Steps: Pursue an MBA or PG Diploma in Corporate Communications.

Brand_Image_PR.title: The Vibe Creator (Brand Image / Social Media PR)
Brand_Image_PR.primary_match_text: You sit exactly where strategy meets art. You have an incredible sense of aesthetics, words, and how things 'feel'. You know how to make a boring brand look incredibly cool, premium, and loved by the public.
Brand_Image_PR.day_in_the_life: Designing aesthetic social media campaigns, writing witty comebacks on Twitter, drafting heartfelt apology letters for brands, and curating the perfect Instagram grid.
Brand_Image_PR.alternative_match_text: If not PR, your creative flair would make you a brilliant Copywriter, Creative Director, or UI/UX Designer.
Brand_Image_PR.roadmap: 11th/12th: Arts or Commerce. Degree: Bachelor of Mass Media (BMM), B.A. in Media Studies, or B.Des. Next Steps: Specialize in Digital Marketing or Brand Management.

PR_Director.title: The Image Boss (PR Director / Celebrity Manager)
PR_Director.primary_match_text: You are a master strategist and a natural leader. You understand human psychology, but you focus on the big picture: reputation, money, and power. You know how to make people into superstars.
PR_Director.day_in_the_life: Representing top Bollywood stars or CEOs, negotiating million-rupee brand deals, deciding which interviews your client should accept, and guiding their long-term public image.
PR_Director.alternative_match_text: Your leadership and negotiation skills would make you an excellent Talent Agent, Entrepreneur, or Marketing Head.
PR_Director.roadmap: 11th/12th: Commerce or Arts. Degree: BBA or B.Com. Next Steps: Work in an agency for a few years, then crack CAT/GMAT and get an MBA in Marketing or PR from a top-tier institute.
